

**Mechanistic Analysis of Over-Squashing and Attention Dilution in Hybrid Graph Neural Networks**

Supervisor: Dr. Greg Green

# **Abstract**

Graph Neural Networks face two related but distinct failure modes when learning long-range dependencies. Message-passing models can suffer from over-squashing, where information from distant nodes is compressed through structural bottlenecks. Graph Transformers can avoid those bottlenecks through global attention, but they may suffer from attention dilution when weight spreads thinly across many irrelevant nodes. Hybrid architectures such as GPS are designed to combine local message passing with global attention, yet practitioners still lack guidance for deciding when local, global, or hybrid models are most appropriate.

This proposal develops a mechanistic framework for architecture selection. Over-squashing is diagnosed with effective resistance and Jacobian sensitivity, while dilution is diagnosed with normalized attention entropy. Three pilot experiments support the framework: a Reddit subreddit graph experiment comparing GraphSAGE with a virtual-master-node hybrid; a Peptides-func replication under the Tönshoff training recipe; and direct measurement of Jacobian sensitivity and attention entropy across GINE, Graph Transformer, and GPS models. The final output will be a two-axis phase diagram mapping effective resistance and dilution exposure to the architecture class most likely to work well.

Keywords: graph neural networks, over-squashing, attention dilution, effective resistance, Graph Transformers, GPS, Long-Range Graph Benchmark

# **1\. Introduction and Problem Statement**

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are widely used for relational data, including molecular property prediction, fraud detection, recommendation systems, and social-network modeling. In these settings, the relationships among entities often contain as much signal as the entities themselves. However, choosing the right GNN architecture remains mostly empirical. Practitioners typically train a local message-passing model, a Graph Transformer, and a hybrid model, then select the best validation result. This workflow is expensive and does not explain why one architecture works better than another.

The core difficulty is that long-range graph learning is limited by at least two different mechanisms. Over-squashing occurs when many distant signals must pass through a narrow structural bottleneck, causing message-passing networks to lose information. Recent theory connects this phenomenon to effective resistance: pairs of nodes with high effective resistance are harder for local message passing to communicate across. Attention dilution is the complementary failure mode for global attention. Although attention gives every node direct access to every other node, it can spread probability mass too uniformly as graph size grows, reducing focus on task-relevant nodes.

Hybrid models such as GPS combine a message-passing branch with a global-attention branch, but their success should not be treated as automatic. On some graphs, the local branch may be sufficient; on others, global attention may help overcome structural bottlenecks; and on large noisy graphs, global attention may introduce dilution. This project asks a practical question: can we diagnose the binding constraint from graph structure and model measurements before relying only on trial-and-error training?

# **2\. Research Goals and Scope**

The main goal is to build a quantitative framework that maps graph structure and model behavior to architecture choice. Instead of reporting only aggregate accuracy, the project measures the mechanisms that should cause success or failure. Over-squashing is measured through effective resistance and Jacobian sensitivity. Attention dilution is measured through attention entropy normalized by graph size. These quantities can be computed on real datasets and trained models, making the framework useful beyond synthetic benchmarks.

The empirical work has three goals. First, on a real social graph, the project tests whether adding a long-range shortcut helps most on nodes far from the training anchor, which would indicate over-squashing. Second, on LRGB Peptides-func, the project replicates a tuned GCN-versus-GPS comparison so that later mechanistic measurements are grounded in a clean training regime. Third, the project measures Jacobian-versus-effective-resistance slopes and attention-entropy-versus-graph-size trends directly on trained GINE, Graph Transformer, and GPS models.

The scope is intentionally bounded. The work compares local models, global attention models, and GPS-style hybrids on two real datasets: the Reddit subreddit graph and Peptides-func. It does not train large graph foundation models or every sparse-attention variant. Exphormer and GRIT are discussed as related work, but GPS is the main hybrid architecture studied. Compute is limited to experiments feasible on a single consumer-grade GPU.

# **3\. Background and Related Work**

Over-squashing was introduced as a limitation of message-passing GNNs: information from exponentially many distant nodes can be compressed into fixed-size hidden states at bottleneck nodes. Di Giovanni et al. later connected this limitation to effective resistance, showing that Jacobian sensitivity between two nodes is bounded by graph topology. This makes effective resistance an attractive diagnostic because it can be calculated directly from the graph Laplacian and interpreted as a structural communication difficulty.

Graph Transformers were developed partly to avoid this bottleneck by replacing local message passing with global self-attention. Graphormer and related architectures showed that attention can work well on graphs when paired with structural or positional encodings, such as degree information, shortest-path distances, Laplacian encodings, or Random Walk Structural Encodings (RWSE). Without such encodings, vanilla attention often lacks the inductive bias needed for graph structure.

Hybrid architectures combine these ideas. GPS applies a local message-passing branch and a global attention branch in each layer, allowing the model to preserve local chemical or neighborhood structure while also enabling long-range communication. However, recent work by Tönshoff et al. showed that carefully tuned message-passing networks can close much of the reported gap on the Long-Range Graph Benchmark. This finding motivates the central question of this proposal: not whether attention helps on average, but when attention provides an irreducible benefit.

Attention dilution is less established in graph learning than over-squashing, but it is closely related to long-context behavior in language models. As context size grows, attention may become less focused on the relevant token or node. In graphs, the analogous measurement is the entropy of each node attention distribution, normalized by the logarithm of graph size. Values near one indicate nearly uniform attention and therefore high dilution exposure.

# **4\. Data**

The project uses two datasets because they represent different graph-learning regimes. The Reddit subreddit graph is a sparse social graph with approximately twenty thousand nodes. Nodes represent subreddits, edges encode cross-posting or user-overlap relations, and node features are based on LIWC psycholinguistic categories. The task is node-level regression: predicting one feature from the remaining features. Train, validation, and test sets are defined by BFS distance from the highest-out-degree anchor node. Nodes within zero or one hop are used for training, nodes at two hops for validation, and nodes at three or more hops for testing. This split directly stresses long-range generalization.

The second dataset is LRGB Peptides-func, a benchmark of roughly fifteen thousand peptide molecular graphs with ten binary functional labels per graph. The standard evaluation metric is multi-label Average Precision. This dataset is useful because it combines local chemistry with global molecular structure and has established published baselines. Its variation in graph size also supports testing whether attention entropy increases as the number of nodes grows.

# **5\. Methodology**

The methodology follows three principles. First, performance is stratified by structural difficulty rather than summarized only with one aggregate metric. On Reddit, the structural axis is BFS distance from the anchor. On Peptides-func, the axis is average effective resistance. Second, the project measures mechanisms directly on trained models: Jacobian sensitivity for over-squashing and normalized attention entropy for dilution. Third, model comparisons are controlled by using shared training settings and architecture skeletons whenever possible.

## **5.1 Feature and Structural Processing**

For Reddit, the 86-dimensional LIWC vector is split into an input set and a regression target. Standardization uses only training-node statistics to avoid leakage. BFS distances are computed on a symmetrized graph, while supervision is limited to real-source nodes. For Peptides-func, atom and bond features are encoded with standard LRGB encoders, and RWSE with walk length twenty is used as positional information. Effective resistance is computed from the Moore-Penrose pseudo-inverse of the graph Laplacian on connected components of valid size.

## **5.2 Model Classes**

Three model classes are compared. The local class uses GraphSAGE on Reddit and GINE on Peptides-func. These models rely on message passing and are expected to be most vulnerable to over-squashing. The global class is a Graph Transformer using multi-head self-attention. It should avoid local bottlenecks but may suffer attention dilution. The hybrid class is GPS, which combines a GINE branch with a global attention branch. In the mechanistic experiment, the three architectures share the same hidden dimension, number of layers, dropout, and readout head as much as possible.

**Table 1\.** *Classes of Graphical Models*

| Class | Representative model | Mechanism | Main risk |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Local | GraphSAGE / GINE | Message passing | Over-squashing |
| Global | Graph Transformer | Full self-attention | Attention dilution |
| Hybrid | GPS | MPNN \+ attention | Both risks, partly mitigated |

## **5.3 Experiments**

Experiment 1 tests over-squashing on Reddit. A three-layer GraphSAGE model is compared with the same backbone augmented by a virtual master node connected to all real nodes. Because the test set begins at distance three, this design checks whether a shortcut improves performance most where long-range communication is hardest. Results are reported as test MSE by distance band and compared with a constant-predictor baseline.

**Figure 1\.** *MSE at increasing distances*

![][image1]

**Figure 2\.** *Standard deviation of MSE*

![][image2]

Experiment 2 replicates the Peptides-func GCN-versus-GPS comparison under the Tönshoff training recipe. The goal is not to maximize benchmark performance but to establish a reliable training setup before interpreting mechanistic measurements. Average Precision on the validation set selects the best epoch, and test Average Precision is reported for the chosen model.

Experiment 3 measures mechanisms directly. For over-squashing, the project samples node pairs across effective-resistance quantiles and computes the Frobenius norm of the Jacobian sensitivity between input and final node embedding. A negative log-log slope between sensitivity and effective resistance is interpreted as an over-squashing signature. For dilution, cached attention weights are converted into per-graph entropy and normalized by log graph size. A positive relationship between normalized entropy and graph size is interpreted as dilution exposure.

**Figure 3\.** *Jacobian Sensitivity across architectures*

![][image3]

**Figure 4\.** *Attention and entropy across graph sizes*

![][image4]

A final synthetic-graph suite will provide controlled validation. Bottleneck experiments will vary graph diameter and communication paths while holding other factors fixed. Dilution experiments will inject task-irrelevant distractor nodes under random and clustered regimes. These controlled settings will test whether the same diagnostics used on real graphs recover the intended failure mode.

# **6\. Preliminary Findings**

The three pilot experiments support the proposed framework, although full multi-seed confirmation remains unfinished. On Reddit, the virtual-master-node hybrid reduces error more strongly at larger BFS distances than at near distances. This pattern is consistent with over-squashing: the shortcut matters most where a local model must communicate through longer and narrower paths.

On Peptides-func, the replication confirms the recent literature’s qualitative result that a tuned message-passing baseline can perform close to GPS. This is important because it prevents the project from overstating the value of attention based only on aggregate performance. If GCN or GINE and GPS achieve similar Average Precision, the mechanistic measurements become more important, not less, because they show whether similar performance comes from different underlying behavior.

The direct measurements show the clearest mechanistic signal. GINE produces a negative Jacobian-versus-effective-resistance slope, the Graph Transformer produces a much flatter slope, and GPS lies between the two. This matches the expectation that message passing is most sensitive to structural bottlenecks, attention bypasses them, and the hybrid partially mitigates them. Attention entropy also increases with graph size for attention-based models, which supports the dilution hypothesis. GPS shows lower raw entropy than the pure Graph Transformer, suggesting that its local branch may reduce the burden on global attention.

**Table 2\.** *Experiments and Observations*

| Experiment | Measurement | Interpretation | Observed direction |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Reddit | MSE by BFS distance | Over-squashing at long range | Supports hypothesis |
| Peptides-func | Test Average Precision | Aggregate benchmark behavior | Narrowed GCN-GPS gap |
| Peptides-func | Jacobian vs. effective resistance | Over-squashing signature | Supports hypothesis |
| Peptides-func | Entropy / log N | Attention dilution signature | Supports hypothesis |

# **7\. Discussion, Limitations, and Remaining Work**

The preliminary results suggest that over-squashing and attention dilution are measurable on real datasets, not only on synthetic graphs. The Reddit experiment shows that distance-dependent error gaps can appear in a naturally occurring social graph. The Peptides-func experiments show that aggregate metrics can hide mechanistic differences: two models may have similar Average Precision while still relying on different communication mechanisms.

Several limitations remain. The mechanistic measurements were pilot runs and need three-seed replication for stable confidence intervals. The Graph Transformer configuration must include positional encodings in the final version, since attention without structure is a weak baseline. Effective resistance and graph size are correlated on molecular graphs, so the final analysis should include size-controlled regression to separate resistance effects from simple graph-scale effects. Finally, the synthetic ablations are still needed to isolate cause from correlation.

The remaining work has three parts. First, complete the synthetic bottleneck and dilution experiments. Second, repeat the Peptides-func experiments across multiple seeds and depth settings. Third, validate the framework on Peptides-struct and convert the empirical results into a practical phase diagram. The final deliverable will be an architecture-selection guide: high effective resistance should favor shortcuts or hybrid attention; high dilution exposure should favor locality-biased models or sparse attention; and intermediate cases should favor GPS-style hybrids.

# **8\. Conclusion**

This proposal reframes GNN architecture selection as a mechanistic diagnosis problem. Instead of asking only which model has the best validation metric, it asks whether the task is limited by over-squashing, attention dilution, or both. Effective resistance and Jacobian sensitivity diagnose structural bottlenecks, while normalized attention entropy diagnoses dilution. The pilot experiments on Reddit and Peptides-func provide early evidence that these measurements align with architecture behavior. After multi-seed replication and controlled synthetic validation, the project will produce a phase diagram that gives practitioners a principled way to choose among local, global, and hybrid graph architectures.
